header:
Date: 2027-04-10
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE); Priya Anand (Redwood SE); Marcus Lee (CTO, Sable Tech); Aisha Patel (Head of Security, Sable Tech); Nora Kim (Platform Engineer, Sable Tech)
summary: Initial security posture discovery focused on whether Sable Tech will use Redwood hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Main concerns: SOC 2 & ISO certifications, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC, audit logs and retention, encryption/KMS options, data residency, and contractual requirements for retention and deletion. Redwood AE/SE to provide compliance docs and VPC/network diagram; plan a Dedicated benchmark for latency and a follow-up on VPC technical details.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood — with me is Priya our SE. Quick intro?
[00:10] Marcus: Marcus here, CTO at Sable Tech. Aisha, Head of Security, and Nora from platform are on.
[00:18] Aisha: Hi. We're primarily evaluating security posture for any vendor we put inference onto.
[00:25] Priya: Great, thanks. Today we'll run through our compliance suite and deployment options — hosted, dedicated, private — and answer your questions on SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS, retention.
[00:40] Marcus: High level: we have PHI-ish telemetry and some PII, so we need strong guarantees. We prefer not to self-host initially. Curious what caveats exist on hosted.
[00:50] Jordan: Totally. Hosted is quickest to go live but we understand concerns. We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 attestation — we'll share the reports under NDA. For highly sensitive workloads customers move to Dedicated or Private, but hosted can meet many controls.
[01:05] Aisha: When you say 'attestation', is that the actual report or a summary? We need the full Type II report redacted is fine.
[01:12] Jordan: Full Type II report, redacted where necessary. We'll send it.
[01:18] Nora: Network wise, if hosted, how does traffic traverse? Do you support VPC peering or private link?
[01:27] Priya: Good question. For hosted we offer PrivateLink and customer VPC peering in certain regions; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with customer VPC option, and Private is fully customer-managed network. We'll send the network diagram and options.
[01:40] Marcus: For Dedicated — is the control plane still Redwood-managed? How much access do we get to logs?
[01:47] Jordan: For Dedicated the control plane remains managed but with isolated tenant resources. You get comprehensive audit logs — token-level and per-route — and can stream logs to your SIEM via syslog or S3 export.
[01:57] Aisha: We need immutable audit logs with tamper-evidence and retention options up to seven years for certain workflows. Can you support WORM-like storage or CDC to our storage?
[02:07] Priya: We currently support streaming audit events to your S3 buckets with versioning and lifecycle rules; customers implement WORM on their end. We can also integrate with partner log stores. For tamper-evidence we provide signed log bundles and retention metadata. I'll add specifics in the doc.
[02:25] Marcus: Encryption at rest — do you use customer-managed keys?
[02:28] Jordan: Yes, for Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed KMS/HSM. For hosted we offer platform-managed keys by default and bring-your-own-key (BYOK) in enterprise tiers.
[02:38] Aisha: Is the BYOK true envelope encryption with separate keys per customer? And can keys be rotated without downtime?
[02:44] Priya: It's envelope encryption — yes separate CMKs per customer for BYOK. Key rotation is supported; we have processes to rotate without impacting live requests by maintaining key versions for decryption of cached data, though we'll document potential short windows.
[02:58] Nora: About caching — you mentioned KV cache in the docs. If we put PII in prompts, how is cached data protected or redacted?
[03:07] Priya: We recommend application-side redaction for PII before sending. On our side, prefix/KV cache can be disabled per-tenant or encrypted with customer keys in Dedicated/Private. For hosted we have configurable retention windows and purge APIs.
[03:24] Marcus: Ok. SSO: we run Okta and Azure AD. Do you support SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning?
[03:31] Jordan: Yes SAML 2.0 SSO is supported and SCIM provisioning for users and groups. RBAC is configurable per team and per-route.
[03:40] Aisha: On RBAC, do you have fine-grained roles for model deployment vs billing vs audit access? We need separation of duties.
[03:48] Priya: Yes, we support role templates and custom roles — separation between deployment, billing, observability, and audit. We can also integrate with your IdP for attribute-based access control.
[03:58] Marcus: Any FedRAMP or other government certifications?
[04:01] Jordan: Not FedRAMP. We do SOC 2 and ISO 27001; for more regulated workloads customers typically go Private/on-prem.
[04:09] Aisha: Data residency — we need all inference logs and stored artifacts to remain in EU region for certain customers. Is region pinning available?
[04:16] Priya: Yes, region pinning and model routing by region are supported. We can ensure data-at-rest and logs stay within specified cloud region; Dedicated gives stronger assurances.
[04:26] Marcus: Contracts: we have specific deletion windows and need proof of deletion on contract termination. How do you handle data deletion guarantees?
[04:34] Jordan: We provide deletion APIs, and for Dedicated/Private we can provide certificate of deletion and the ability to wipe caches and volumes. For hosted, there are documented processes and we can include contractual SLA language for deletion.
[04:46] Aisha: Auditability: do you expose the sequence of actions (who called what model, tokens used, input hashes) in the audit logs? We can't store raw PII but need forensic capability.
[04:56] Priya: Audit logs include request metadata, hashed inputs if requested, response metadata, timestamps, and model/version used. You can opt-in for payload hash logs instead of raw payloads.
[05:08] Nora: About performance benchmarks — we need a baseline for 99th percentile latency for 512 token sequences. Can you run that on Dedicated?
[05:15] Priya: Yes, we can run a Dedicated-mode benchmark with your sample prompt set. We'll need a short PoC agreement and a sample corpus. We'll schedule with you.
[05:23] Marcus: Cost/latency tradeoffs — curious about quantization and how it affects accuracy.
[05:29] Jordan: We provide quantized model variants and recommend A/B testing. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles by workload. We'll include guidance and evals.
[05:38] Aisha: Any known gaps from a compliance standpoint? For example, does Redwood support customer-managed PKI for mutual TLS?
[05:44] Priya: Mutual TLS is supported; customers can bring certs and configure mTLS for Dedicated/Private endpoints. For hosted, mTLS is possible through private link + custom certs in enterprise tiers.
[05:56] Marcus: Legal — do you have standard DPA templates and data processing addendums?
[06:00] Jordan: Yes, standard DPA and privacy addendum. We also have data processing terms for EU data residency. We'll send the DPA and suggested edits if needed.
[06:10] Aisha: For compliance evidence, can we get the list of sub-processors and their locations?
[06:14] Jordan: Absolutely — we'll include the current sub-processor list and region mapping.
[06:19] Nora: On logging volume — we expect high event rates, how does Redwood handle retention costs and log shipping throughput?
[06:27] Priya: We support streaming with partitioning and batching; you can set retention policies and lifecycle rules on your S3. For hosted customers we provide token-level cost views so you can see logging costs.
[06:40] Marcus: What's a typical timeline to go from PoC to Dedicated?
[06:44] Jordan: For Dedicated it's usually 4–8 weeks depending on compliance reviews and network setup; Private/on-prem is longer. PoC bench can be done in 1–2 weeks.
[06:53] Aisha: Can you commit to pen test or will you accept our third-party assessor?
[06:58] Priya: We do annual internal and external pen tests and can accept third-party assessments under NDA and scheduling.
[07:07] Marcus: Great. Next steps?
[07:09] Jordan: We'll send SOC 2 and ISO artifacts, DPA, sub-processor list, VPC diagram, and pricing. Priya will prepare a Dedicated benchmark plan.
[07:17] Aisha: We'll provide data residency and retention policy and sample prompts for the benchmark.
[07:23] Jordan: Perfect. We'll follow up with dates. Thanks all.
[07:27] End of recording.

Notes about transcription: occasional overlaps and mis-typed product names (e.g., 'private link' transcribed as 'private link' sometimes capitalized), pauses, and filler words retained. Some technical nouns may be slightly mis-spelled in auto transcript (KMS sometimes 'K M S').
